{{short description|Italian astrophysicist|bot=PearBOT 5}}
'''Enrico Costa''' (born 1944 in [[Sassari]], [[Sardinia]]) is an Italian astrophysicist, known for studies of [[gamma ray burst]]s (GRBs).

Costa's family moved in 1954 to Rome, where he spent the remainder of his childhood and adolescence and studied physics. For his PhD with Giulio Auriemma, he participated in rocket experiments with X-ray detectors at the IAS (Istituto di Astrofisica Spaziale) in Rome. In 1976, he joined the IAS and worked on balloon experiments. Later he was involved in [[BeppoSAX]], the Italian X-ray astronomy satellite (with Dutch participation, and [[European Space Agency|ESA]] support), which operated from 1996 to 2003. Costa was in 1981 part of the team of Livio Scarsi, which proposed the construction of the satellite for X-ray detection. On the satellite was a [[Phoswich Detector]]<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.detectors.saint-gobain.com/Phoswich.aspx |title=Phoswich "phosphor sandwich" detector description from Saint Gobain Crystals |access-date=2012-06-14 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130104154922/http://www.detectors.saint-gobain.com/Phoswich.aspx |archive-date=2013-01-04 |url-status=dead }}</ref> System (PDS) used by Filippo Frontera for the discovery of gamma ray bursts (i.e., the PDS was a Gamma Ray Burst Monitor, GRBM). February 28, 1997 was the first time an X-ray afterglow associated with a GRB was observed after localization by SAX,<ref>[http://www.cbat.eps.harvard.edu/iauc/06500/06572.html message of GRB 970228 to the IAU by Costa and others]. Costa, Frontera, et al. ''Discovery of an X-ray afterglow associated with the γ-ray burst of 28 February 1997'', Nature, Vol. 387, 1997, pp.783–785, [https://arxiv.org/abs/astro-ph/9706065 Arxiv]</ref> followed shortly thereafter by the optical afterglow (observed by Herschel and Isaac Newton telescopes, [[La Palma]]). Two months later, another GRB was detected with subsequent observation in the radio range, thus directly demonstrating by the redshift that GRBs are of extragalactic origin.<ref>[https://arxiv.org/abs/astro-ph/9712134 Daniel Reichert ''The redshift of GRB 970580'', Astrophysical Journal Letters, Volume 495, 1997, pp. L99-L101]</ref> In 1999, he developed the X-ray detector for the Italian X-ray/gamma-ray satellites [[AGILE (spacecraft)|AGILE]], which started in 2007. He also developed X-ray [[polarimeter]]s.

Enrico Costa is the author or co-author of a number of papers in peer reviewed scientific journals. Several are published in Science Magazine.<ref>{{cite web
 | title =Costa's body of work
 | publisher =Google Scholar
 | url =https://scholar.google.com/scholar?start=0&q=Enrico+Costa&hl=en&as_sdt=0,22
 | format =Web page with links to papers and citations
 | access-date =2012-06-15}}</ref> Also, in 2011 he received with [[Gerald J. Fishman]] the [[Shaw Prize]].
